module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 899

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/899](https://www.erdosproblems.com/899)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter Set

open scoped Pointwise Topology

namespace Erdos899

open Erdos899

/--
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set such that $|A\cap \{1, ..., N\}| = o(N)$.
Is it true that
$$
\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac{|(A - A)\cap \{1, ..., N\}|}{|A \cap \{1, ..., N\}|} = \infty?
$$

The answer is yes, proved by Ruzsa [Ru78].

[Ru78] Ruzsa, I. Z., _On the cardinality of {$A+A$}\ and {$A-A$}_. (1978), 933--938.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/dfe2d78128b493c572cf525b1b8edf4897fb7664/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos899.lean#L793"]
theorem erdos_899 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ (A : Set ℕ), A.Infinite →
    Tendsto (fun N => (A ∩ Icc 1 N |>.ncard : ℝ) / N) atTop (𝓝 0) →
    atTop.limsup (fun N => ((A - A : Set ℕ) ∩ Icc 1 N |>.ncard : EReal) /
      (A ∩ Icc 1 N).ncard) = ⊤ := by
  sorry

end Erdos899

reformulations.difference: The difference set uses pointwise truncated subtraction on ℕ rather than integer subtraction.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every positive natural d, a - b = d in ℕ iff (a : ℤ) - (b : ℤ) = (d : ℤ). Consequently, casting into ℤ identifies the natural-number difference set intersected with Icc 1 N with the integer difference set intersected with the same interval. The extra zero values from truncated subtraction are excluded. The counted sets therefore have identical cardinalities for every N, so the limsup claims are equivalent. Both the cardinality identity and the conclusion-level ↔ were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without sorry dependencies.
